title: Enterprise Prospect Playbook: Positioning, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Lina Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook is designed to equip Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, and Sales Engineering with a single, production-ready reference for engaging enterprise prospects. It combines core positioning and messaging, concise competitor brief(s), a recommended pitch deck outline with ROI examples, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, three short anonymized case studies, and a prospect-focused security FAQ. Use the ‘Quick Win’ and ‘Technical Deep Dive’ sections to tailor conversations for executive and technical stakeholders respectively.

1) Core positioning and messaging (elevator to executive):

- Headline: Redwood Inference — predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference that’s production-ready across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Value pillars (1-liners):
  - Performance predictability: SLA-backed dedicated capacity and observability to guarantee latency/throughput targets.
  - Cost control: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles that reduce per-token costs by up to 4x in many workloads.
  - Deployment flexibility & security: same API and controls from hosted to VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads.
  - Developer-first experience: fast SDKs, debug-friendly tracing, and built-in evals for quality guardrails.
- Primary pitch themes by persona:
  - Engineering/ML: "Keep inference predictable without building a custom runtime — we manage kernels, batching, and KV cache so your models run efficiently at scale."
  - Platform/SRE: "Single control plane for routing, tracing, and capacity planning with clear SLOs and error budgets — reduces operational toil."
  - Procurement/Security: "Private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logging that match enterprise compliance requirements."

2) Competitive brief (one-page summary for deal prep):

- Competitors covered: Open LLM API providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic), cloud managed endpoints (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex), and inference infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes, third-party orchestration).
- Typical competitor strengths and our responses:
  - Open LLM APIs: Strength — fastest time-to-value, large model selection. Risk — unpredictable unit economics at scale and limited deployment control.
    - Our counter: Hosted API to match time-to-value, plus Dedicated & Private for predictable unit economics and data isolation. Offer migration playbook and clear benchmarking.
  - Cloud managed endpoints (SageMaker/Vertex): Strength — deep cloud integrations. Risk — vendor lock-in, less inference-specific optimizations.
    - Our counter: Multi-cloud routing and optimized serving kernels tuned for throughput/latency; emphasize cost/performance benchmarks on comparable hardware.
  - Self-hosted inference stacks: Strength — full control. Risk — high ops burden and slower iteration.
    - Our counter: Provide Private deployment + managed control plane option and on-prem packaging to reduce ops burden; show TCO comparison (engineering hours + infra) vs. self-build.

Quick competitive win themes:
- When prospect cares strongly about cost-per-token predictability -> emphasize Dedicated and Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quant profiles).
- When prospect needs strict isolation and policy controls -> emphasize Private deployment and KMS/HSM integrations with audit logs.
- When prospect prioritizes developer productivity -> show SDKs, evals, and plug-and-play rollouts with A/B/canary.

3) Pitch deck outline (recommended slide flow):

- Slide 0: Title / Customer name / Meeting objective.
- Slide 1: Executive summary — problem, Redwood value prop, top-line ROI/metric.
- Slide 2: Customer pain (latency variability, runaway token spend, ops burden, compliance risk).
- Slide 3: How Redwood solves it (hosted, dedicated, private + console).
- Slide 4: Technical deep dive (runtime, kernel selection, caching, routing).
- Slide 5: Cost comparison vs. status quo (example workloads).
- Slide 6: Reliability & SLAs (uptime %, p99 latencies, error budget handling).
- Slide 7: Security & compliance (SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM, VPC).
- Slide 8: Rollout plan & resources (pilot → scale → dedicated → private if required).
- Slide 9: Case study highlights.
- Slide 10: Commercials & next steps.

Pitching tips:
- Early meetings: lead with a short benchmark demo showing 95th percentile latency and per-1M token cost under two modes (hosted vs dedicated).
- Technical meetings: bring an SE to review model trace, KV cache hit rate, estimated batching improvements for their prompt distribution.
- Economic conversations: use a per-request and per-month "sample workload" calc (see ROI example below).

ROI example (single-calc template):
- Inputs (example): 100M tokens/month; average generation length 50 tokens; current provider cost $0.0015/token.
- Current cost: 100M * $0.0015 = $150,000/month.
- Redwood projected: with batching and quantization -> 40% unit cost reduction -> $0.0009/token => $90,000/month.
- Additional savings: prefix caching and reuse can reduce active tokens by 15% -> effective monthly cost ~$76,500.
- Non-monetary upside: reduced p99 latency from 800ms to 200ms -> better UX and higher retention for end-users.

4) Pricing guidance & negotiation levers (SDR/AEs):

- Pricing building blocks (hosted):
  - Per-token generation rate (tiered by volume), per-embedding unit, and optional retention/observability add-ons.
  - Typical mid-market reference: $0.0008–$0.0015 per generated token depending on model tier and volume.
- Dedicated / Reserved capacity:
  - Monthly reservation with commit tiers and burst allowances. Minimums vary by region and GPU class; typical enterprise starting contract: $20k–$60k/month depending on model family and throughput.
  - Discounts: 10–30% depending on term length (12/24/36 months) and committed spend.
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem):
  - Platform fee + professional services. Platform fee typically negotiated as annual license; PS scoped per deployment (typical PS: 4–12 weeks).
- Commercial levers to negotiate:
  1) Term length and committed $ -> drives % discount.
  2) Model family selection & quantization profile -> lower-cost model variants can be offered as fallback to reduce unit rates.
  3) Observability retention and SLA tiers -> chargeable add-ons.
  4) Professional services for migration, latency tuning, or on-prem packaging.
- Helpful talk tracks: outline the incremental roadmap (pilot -> throughput targets -> SLA-backed Dedicated) and the financial kicker: commit to X tokens/month at Y discount for guaranteed capacity and predictable per-token rates.

5) Case studies (anonymized, to use in sales collateral):

- FinSight (SaaS financial insights platform) — Outcome:
  - Challenge: inconsistent p99 latency and unpredictable token spend during peak analytics periods.
  - Redwood solution: migrated to Dedicated capacity + KV caching and tuned quant profile.
  - Result: p99 day-of-week latency reduced from 900ms to 220ms; monthly inference costs down 38%; time-to-detect model regressions improved with built-in evals.

- ShopAssist (eCommerce personalization engine) — Outcome:
  - Challenge: scaling chat personalization to 10k concurrent sessions; on-prem requirement for PII handling.
  - Redwood solution: Private deployment with customer-managed VPC + KMS integration and audit logging; rollout with canary traffic slicing.
  - Result: customer met compliance needs and achieved 2.5x throughput on GPU T4-equivalent nodes via batching and kernel tuning; reduced devops overhead vs self-hosted alternative.

- Parcelly (logistics routing & assistant) — Outcome:
  - Challenge: high unit cost during peak routing queries and requirement for sub-200ms tail latency.
  - Redwood solution: use of Dedicated pools, model variant routing (high-cost low-latency vs low-cost high-throughput), and aggressive prefix caching.
  - Result: 45% reduction in peak hourly spend and consistent p99 < 200ms during business hours.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise, suitable for RFP responses):

- Q: Where is customer data stored and can we enforce region-only residency?
  - A: For Hosted customers we support region-restricted storage in primary cloud regions in NA, EU, and APAC. Dedicated and Private deployments keep all inference and logs inside the customer VPC or on-premise environment.

- Q: How is data encrypted?
  - A: Encryption in transit with TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 and encryption at-rest using cloud provider KMS by default. For Private deployments we integrate with customer-managed KMS or HSM for key custody.

- Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) / HSM?
  - A: Yes. Dedicated and Private deployments support CMKs and HSM-backed key stores; Hosted customers may choose a managed KMS option or enter a custom agreement for CMK in select regions.

- Q: What compliance standards do you meet?
  - A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. We provide artifacts and standard questionnaires for due diligence. For enterprise deals we provide tailored compliance evidence packages.

- Q: How do you handle model data leakage and prompt privacy?
  - A: We provide options to disable training/retention of prompts on hosted tiers and guarantee that customer inputs and outputs for Dedicated/Private are never used for model training. We also provide masking patterns and prompt redaction tooling in the Console.

- Q: What audit capabilities exist?
  - A: Audit logs include API keys used, route, model version, timestamps, and traces. Logs are exportable to SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, S3) or retained in-customer VPC for Private deployments.

- Q: How is access control enforced?
  - A: Role-based access control (RBAC) in the Console, integration with SSO (SAML/OIDC), and strict key management for API keys. Dedicated and Private support fine-grained token scoping for route-level controls.

- Q: Incident response and breach notification?
  - A: Standard incident playbook with SLA-based notification windows. Enterprise contracts include breach notification timelines and joint tabletop exercises on request.

7) Objection handling cheatsheet (short):

- "Your price is higher than public API": explain predictable TCO over spikes, show sample workload calc, offer pilot credits for evaluation.
- "We want to self-host for control": explain hidden ops costs and offer Private deployment with managed control plane or a co-managed option.
- "We’re worried about model regressions": emphasize built-in evals, quality guardrails, and regression triage processes.

8) Playbook operational checklist (for AE/SE to run a winning pilot):

1. Agree success metrics (latency, throughput, token spend) and dataset for evals.
2. Provision pilot environment (Hosted or Dedicated sandbox) and share API credentials & sample prompts.
3. Run 2-week benchmark: baseline (current provider) vs Redwood with default optimize settings.
4. Share consolidated benchmark deck (latency p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, KV cache hit rate).
5. Tune: adjust batch targets, quantization profile, and model variant routing for target SLOs.
6. Present final recommendation and commercialization options (Dedicated/Private proposals).

Owners and maintenance:
